newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says army wins back southeastern town.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says army wins back southeastern town.

text.p: The Sudanese army has recaptured the southeastern town of Chali el-Fil from the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), which took the town in January, President Omar Hassan al-Bashir said on Sunday.
Lieutenant-General Bashir announced the military success at a rally called to denounce what the government says was a Ugandan attack on two southern towns last week.
"This is the beginning. The battles will continue until every inch of our land has been liberated," added Bashir.
Chali el-Fil, in Blue Nile state 30 km (20 miles) from the Ethiopian border, fell to the rebels in a joint offensive by the SPLA and the military wing of northern opposition groups.
Khartoum said Ethiopian and Eritrean troops did most of the fighting but independent observers are sceptical.
The rebels made rapid advances at first in Blue Nile and Kassala states but the campaign soon ran out of steam and a government counter-attack did not materialise for weeks.
The Khartoum government said on Saturday that the army had also recaptured the small town of Boing, just across the state border in Upper Nile to the south.
Chali el-Fil lies 50 km (30 miles) south of the substantial border town of Kurmuk, which the SPLA continues to hold.

For the rally on Sunday, a crowd of thousands gathered outside armed forces headquarters chanting slogans such as "A million martyrs to defend the faith", "Allahu Akbar (God is Greatest)" and "Down with the Zionists".
Speakers attacked the United States, blaming it for the recent attacks near the Ugandan border in the south.
In Nairobi the SPLA said on Sunday that in the south its fighters had captured Lainya, a garrison town on the road to Juba, the main town on the whole of southern Sudan.
"Lainya fell to the SPLA yesterday (Saturday) at 1800 hours local time (1600 GMT)," said SPLA spokesman Samson Kwaje.
He said he received the news from SPLA leader John Garang in the town of Yei but he gave no further details.
Sudanese rebels said on Friday they were advancing towards Lainya after capturing 1,000 government soldiers and a large quantity of weapons when they overran Yei and Morobo garrison.
